intro: Picture a condo where the common areas are turned into a whole zone of tropical pools — waterfalls, a mock cave, a slide, and a water park for kids — right in the Jomtien area, which is far quieter than central Pattaya. Laguna Beach Resort 2 is a large condo resort where many units are rented out by the night through the big booking sites · developed by Vistas Development and completed in 2016, with 8-storey buildings totalling around 1,100 units · rooms are 24 sqm studios with an in-room kitchen and a private balcony, about 600–700 metres' walk to Jomtien Beach · prices start at around THB 700–900/night, and real guest reviews give it about 8.4 on Booking.com — a good fit if you want a great pool and an in-room kitchen on a budget.

body.html: Who Laguna Beach Resort 2 is for — an overview — first, let's be clear: Laguna Beach Resort 2 isn't a hotel with a single front desk running the whole building like a Hilton or a Centara · it's a large condominium development where individual owners bought their units, and many of those units are then rented out by the night through room-management companies such as Pattaya Sunny Rentals, Snap Hosting, GSR, and several others on the big booking sites like Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com · understanding this matters a lot, because it tells you up front that the stay won't be "the same in every room" — it depends on who manages the room you book · so who is this place right for? Real reviews make it fairly clear that the happiest guests are budget travellers who want a nice pool and an in-room kitchen to cook for themselves, couples after somewhere quieter than central Pattaya, families with young kids who want them splashing about in the water park, and remote workers (digital nomads) looking for a longer stay by the week or month at a price they can manage · the people it may not suit are those expecting 5-star hotel service with staff on hand around the clock, because this is a condo that sells privacy and value rather than full-service hospitality.

Location and getting around — Laguna Beach Resort 2 sits in the Nong Prue area, near the northern stretch of Jomtien Beach on the southern side of Pattaya · to be honest, the one thing to flag is that the condo isn't beachfront, but Jomtien Beach is about 600–700 metres away, or roughly an 8–10 minute walk (some reviews and platforms list 1–1.5 kilometres depending on which points you measure between) · that distance is easy enough to walk in the morning or evening, but in the midday heat many people choose to ride a motorbike or hail a songthaew instead · the upside of the location is that it's a fair way from the bustle of central Pattaya and Walking Street, so it's quiet and good for relaxing, while still being close to convenience stores, markets, restaurants, and massage shops · getting to the key spots: central Pattaya and Central Pattaya Beach are about a 15–20 min drive, while the Pattaya Floating Market and Nong Nooch Garden are further south · as for airports, if you fly into Suvarnabhumi it's about 120 kilometres away, roughly a 1.5 to 2 hour drive, while U-Tapao Airport is much closer at about 40 minutes · note that this area has no mass transit like a sky train, so having a rented motorbike or using a ride-hailing app makes getting around far easier.

"Booked a studio online for under a thousand a night, but got a pool as nice as a five-star resort, the kids could splash in the water park all day, and there was a little kitchen for making instant noodles and coffee. Way more than the price suggests — you just have to walk a bit to the beach."

Room types and decor — because this is a condo where each owner decorates their own unit, the interiors vary from room to room: some are freshly done and modern, others are simple and to the original standard · the underlying layouts come in just a few types · the most common is the studio of around 24 sqm, combining the bedroom, sitting area, and a kitchen corner in one room, with a private balcony, an en-suite bathroom with a shower, air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, and a safe · a step up is the one-bedroom of around 36–64 sqm, with the bedroom clearly separated from the living area, suited to couples who want more space or a small family · one thing many reviews agree on is the in-room kitchen with a stove, microwave, kettle, and fridge, which saves a lot on food costs over a longer stay and suits people with certain food allergies or who simply want to cook · another point that earns praise is the view — rooms facing the pool look out over the lovely tropical pool landscape, a selling point hosts often promote as "Pool View" · the honest caveat is that since each room is managed by a different host, the cleaning quality and condition of the furniture vary: some reviews find a spotless room, others find a broken shower or dated fittings — so reading the reviews for "that specific host" before booking matters more than reading the development's combined reviews.

Facilities, pools, and water park — this is the real star of Laguna Beach Resort 2 and the main reason people choose to stay here · the development's common areas were designed with a fully loaded cluster of pools, including a large lagoon pool, an Olympic-style pool for swimming laps, and a tropical-themed pool with waterfalls, a mock cave, and a slide · on top of that there's a water park and a kids' pool that let families with young children play all day without leaving · around the pools there's a pool bar, massage salas, an orchid garden, and green spaces to wander · on the fitness and wellness side there's a gym, sauna, jacuzzi, steam room, and an outdoor bathtub in some zones · there are restaurants, cafés, and a minimart within the development, underground parking, and 24-hour security with key cards and CCTV · the honest thing to know is that, because it's a large condo with a lot of guests, on long weekends or in high season the pools can get "crowded" so you don't get the privacy of a small resort, and some reviews have grumbled that the chlorine in the pools is too strong at certain times · but in terms of pool variety and value for money, the common areas here give you far more than the room rate you pay for.

Food and nearby places to eat — there are restaurants, cafés, and a pool bar within the development, but the real charm of staying in the Jomtien area is the restaurants outside · within walking distance and a short motorbike ride there are plenty of Thai restaurants, seafood spots along Jomtien Beach, Western restaurants, Russian restaurants, and Indian restaurants, because this area has a large resident foreign community · food prices in the Jomtien area are generally cheaper than in central Pattaya, and there's not much overcharging of tourists · what gives Laguna Beach Resort 2 an edge on food is the in-room kitchen — many people choose to buy from a nearby market or supermarket and cook for themselves, especially on longer stays, which cuts costs significantly · in the mornings this development mostly does not include breakfast the way an ordinary hotel would, since it's a condo rental, so anyone who loves a breakfast buffet should be prepared to head out or cook for themselves · for coffee lovers, there are cafés and convenience stores around the development within easy walking distance.

Service and check-in — service is where you should set your expectations most carefully · because each room is run by a different host, check-in varies · some have a reception or office on site, some arrange to meet you to hand over a key or key card, and some use self check-in, sending you a lockbox code by message · the upside is flexibility, and you can usually check in at the agreed time; the downside is that if you get a host who replies slowly or communicates unclearly, arrival can be a hassle · from real reviews, hosts with good ratings tend to earn praise for replying quickly on chat, recommending restaurants and transport, and helping with motorbike rental · hosts with poor reviews tend to be criticised for rooms that don't match the photos, poor cleaning, or being hard to reach · the key lesson is to check the host's name before you book and read the reviews for that host specifically, not just look at the overall Laguna Beach Resort 2 listing, because the experience depends mostly on the host you book with.

Real guest reviews (the good and the bad) — gathered from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com, and Tripadvisor across several rental hosts in the development, the overall picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: the pool cluster is beautiful and varied beyond the price, the water park and slide are great for families with young kids, the in-room kitchen saves money and lets you cook, the Jomtien area is quiet and good for relaxing, the value is excellent for what you get, and you can walk to the beach · on Booking.com the overall score across several rental hosts is around 8.4, with many couples rating it as high as around 9.4 for a two-person trip · on the caveat side: the inconsistency between rooms, because they're managed by different hosts, is what gets mentioned the most, some rooms have a broken shower or dated fittings, the chlorine in the pools is too strong at certain times to the point that some people's skin gets irritated, the pools and lifts are crowded on weekends, the walk to the beach is farther than some expected, and there's noise from neighbours or pool-side activities on some days · overall, most of the complaints can be solved by choosing a well-reviewed host and setting the right expectation that this is a rental condo, not a full-service hotel.

"Stayed two weeks while working online — the Wi-Fi was fine, the kitchen let me cook every day, and a swim in the morning before starting work was bliss · the only downside was that the room I got had weak water pressure in the shower, but I told the host and they helped sort it out. At this price, it's totally fine."

Price comparison and value — the strongest point of Laguna Beach Resort 2 is value for money · nightly rates for a studio can start from around THB 700–900/night in the normal season, rising to around THB 1,200–1,800/night in high season or on long weekends, depending on the host and room size · a one-bedroom or a nice pool-view room may be a little higher · for those staying longer, the monthly rate for a studio is around THB 9,000–11,000/month (excluding water and electricity) for a 1–12 month contract, which is very cheap for the facilities you get · compared with hotels in the same area, THB 700–900/night would normally only get you a budget hotel room without a pool like this and without a kitchen · so if what you value is a nice pool, an in-room kitchen, and a relaxing space on a budget, Laguna Beach Resort 2 is a value pick that's hard to find in Pattaya · but if you'll pay more for full hotel service, breakfast, and the certainty of a consistent room standard, it may be worth choosing an actual hotel at a higher rate.

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, choose a host with good reviews and a high number of reviews, because the experience depends on the host who manages the room more than the development itself · two, read the room details carefully — whether it's a pool view or another view, which floor, and what's in the kitchen — because each room is different · three, ask clearly about how check-in and key collection work in advance, especially if you arrive late · four, be prepared for the roughly 600–700 metre walk to the beach; if you'd rather not walk in the sun, rent a motorbike or use a ride-hailing app · five, if you stay over a long weekend, expect the pools and common areas to be crowded · six, ask clearly about the deposit, cleaning fee, and water and electricity charges before paying, especially for a long stay, so there are no unexpected hidden costs.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Laguna Beach Resort 2 is the best fit for people who want a resort-grade pool and an in-room kitchen on a budget, in the quiet Jomtien area · the cluster of tropical pools with a water park and slide, the in-room kitchen that saves money, and prices that start at just a few hundred baht a night make it good value that's hard to match at the same rate, especially for families with young kids and longer stays · but if you expect the consistent service and room standard of a hotel, want breakfast, or need a beachfront stay where you can step straight onto the sand, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a beachfront resort in the Na Jomtien area instead · the most important key to a great stay here is to choose a well-reviewed host, read the room specs carefully, and set the right expectation that this is a condo resort for rent, not a hotel — get all of that right, and Laguna Beach Resort 2 will be one of the best-value stays you can find in Pattaya.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Laguna Beach Resort 2

faq.q: Is Laguna Beach Resort 2 a hotel or a condo · how do you book?
faq.a: It's a large condominium development where many units are rented out by the night through several room-management companies · you can book through Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com, where you'll see different host names such as by Pattaya Sunny Rentals, by Snap Hosting, GSR, and so on · the experience depends on the host you book with, so read that host's reviews before booking.

faq.q: Where is Laguna Beach Resort 2 · can you walk to the beach?
faq.a: It's in the Nong Prue area, near the northern stretch of Jomtien Beach on the southern side of Pattaya · the condo isn't beachfront, but Jomtien Beach is about 600–700 metres away, or roughly an 8–10 minute walk · central Pattaya is about a 15–20 min drive, and U-Tapao Airport is about 40 minutes away.

faq.q: Does Laguna Beach Resort 2 have a pool and a water park?
faq.a: Yes, and it's the biggest highlight here · the common areas have a large cluster of tropical-style pools — a lagoon pool, an Olympic-style pool, and a themed pool with waterfalls, a mock cave, and a slide, plus a water park and a kids' pool · there's also a gym, sauna, jacuzzi, steam room, pool bar, and an orchid garden.

faq.q: How much does it cost to rent at Laguna Beach Resort 2?
faq.a: Nightly studio rentals start at around THB 700–900/night in the normal season, rising to around THB 1,200–1,800/night in high season or on long weekends, depending on the host and room size · monthly studio rentals are around THB 9,000–11,000/month (excluding water and electricity) · it's worth comparing several hosts across several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Do rooms at Laguna Beach Resort 2 have a kitchen · is breakfast included?
faq.a: Most studios have an in-room kitchen with a stove, microwave, and fridge, so you can cook for yourself — a big saving on longer stays · but breakfast is mostly not included, since these are condo rentals rather than a hotel · there are restaurants, cafés, and convenience stores within walking distance around the development.

faq.q: Who is Laguna Beach Resort 2 for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for budget travellers who want a nice pool and an in-room kitchen, families with young kids who want them to play in the water park, and remote workers on longer stays · if you expect hotel-level service and room standards, want breakfast, or need a beachfront stay, a beachfront resort in the Na Jomtien area may suit you better.
